Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### TL;DR  
The shield layers in the **OpenMapTiles** style look for sprite names **`road-shield-1` … `road-shield-12`** (the exact set that the style ships with).  
All you have to do is make the **road-shield sprite sheet** (`road_shield.json` + `road_shield.png` and the `@2x` versions) available to MapLibre and point the style’s `sprite` property at it. No layer-editing is required.

---

## 1. Which sprite names does the style expect?

OpenMapTiles ships a dedicated sprite called **`road_shield`**.  
Inside that sprite the following icon-image names are referenced (the list is exhaustive for the current style version – newer releases may add a few more, but the pattern stays the same):

| Sprite name | What it is used for |
|-------------|---------------------|
| `road-shield-1` | **US Interstate** (I-xx) |
| `road-shield-2` | **US Highway** (US-xx) |
| `road-shield-3` | **US State** (e.g. CA-1) |
| `road-shield-4` | **US County** (e.g. CR-12) |
| `road-shield-5` | **Canada** (e.g. Hwy-401) |
| `road-shield-6` | **Mexico** (e.g. MX-15) |
| `road-shield-7` | **Europe** (e.g. A-7, B-12) |
| `road-shield-8` | **International** (e.g. E-20) |
| `road-shield-9` | **Other / generic** (e.g. “Route 5” in non-US countries) |
| `road-shield-10` | **Railway** (used by the style for some rail-ref badges) |
| `road-shield-11` | **Ferry** (rare) |
| `road-shield-12` | **Custom / user-defined** (fallback) |

The style’s `icon-image` expression is essentially:

```json
"icon-image": [
  "case",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "US:I"], "road-shield-1",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "US:US"], "road-shield-2",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "US:SR"], "road-shield-3",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "US:CR"], "road-shield-4",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "CA:PR"], "road-shield-5",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "MX:PR"], "road-shield-6",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "EU:EU"], "road-shield-7",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "EU:INT"], "road-shield-8",
  ["==", ["get", "network"], "other"], "road-shield-9",
  /* …fallbacks… */
  "road-shield-12"
]
```

If the sprite sheet is missing, the style still draws the `text-field` (the number you see) but falls back to a **transparent** icon – which is exactly the “bare floating numbers” you’re seeing.

---

## 2. Getting the sprite sheet without touching the style

### 2.1. Download the official sprite

The OpenMapTiles repository already contains the ready-made sprite:

```
https://github.com/openmaptiles/openmaptiles/tree/master/styles/road_shield/sprite
```

You will find four files (plus the optional `road_shield@2x` set for high-DPI displays):

```
road_shield.json
road_shield.png
road_shield@2x.json
road_shield@2x.png
```

### 2.2. Host them where your page can fetch them

You can:

* **Serve them from your own web server** (e.g. `https://mydomain.com/sprites/road_shield.*`), or  
* **Use a CDN** (the OpenMapTiles website hosts a copy at `https://openmaptiles.org/sprites/road_shield`).

Make sure the files are reachable **exactly** with the same base name you will reference in the style (no extra folder segment unless you also change the style’s `sprite` URL).

### 2.3. Point the style at the sprite

When you load the style JSON (either the one you built yourself or the pre-published `openmaptiles.json`), set the `sprite` property to the URL **without the file extension**:

```js
const map = new maplibregl.Map({
  container: 'map',
  style: {
    // …your style JSON (or a URL to it)…
    "sprite": "https://mydomain.com/sprites/road_shield",   // <-- important
    // …rest of the style…
  },
  center: [-122.44, 37.76],
  zoom: 10
});
```

If you are loading the style from a URL that already contains a `sprite` entry, you can simply **override** it at runtime:

```js
fetch('https://example.com/styles/openmaptiles.json')
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(style => {
    style.sprite = 'https://mydomain.com/sprites/road_shield';
    const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style });
  });
```

### 2.4. Verify it works

Open the browser dev-tools → **Network** tab and look for requests like:

```
GET https://mydomain.com/sprites/road_shield.json
GET https://mydomain.com/sprites/road_shield.png
GET https://mydomain.com/sprites/road_shield@2x.json
GET https://mydomain.com/sprites/road_shield@2x.png
```

Both the JSON and PNG must load with a **200** status. After that the shields appear instantly (no page reload needed if you change the `sprite` URL while the map is already instantiated – just call `map.setStyle(style)` again).

---

## 3. Why you don’t need to edit the layers

The shield layers are already written to use the **`road-shield-*`** names.  
All that the style does is:

1. **Read the `network` / `ref` / `ref_length` properties** from the vector tile.
2. **Pick the appropriate sprite name** via the `icon-image` expression shown above.
3. **Render the sprite** behind the `text-field` (the number you already see).

If the sprite sheet is missing, step 3 falls back to a **transparent** image, which is why you only see the number. Supplying the correct sprite sheet restores step 3, and the badge appears automatically.

---

## 4. Quick “copy-and-paste” recipe

```bash
# 1️⃣ Grab the sprite from the repo (or CDN)
mkdir -p public/sprites
cd public/sprites
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/openmaptiles/master/styles/road_shield/sprite/road_shield.json
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/openmaptiles/master/styles/road_shield/sprite/road_shield.png
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/openmaptiles/master/styles/road_shield/sprite/road_shield@2x.json
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/openmaptiles/master/styles/road_shield/sprite/road_shield@2x.png

# 2️⃣ Serve the folder (e.g. with a simple static server)
npx serve public   # or any other static-file server

# 3️⃣ In your MapLibre init code:
const map = new maplibregl.Map({
  container: 'map',
  style: {
    // …your style JSON (or a URL)…
    "sprite": "http://localhost:5000/sprites/road_shield", // <-- note: no .png/.json
    // …
  },
  center: [-95, 38],
  zoom: 4
});
```

That’s it – the interstate, US-highway, state-highway, etc., shields will now show their familiar colored badges with the numbers you already have.

---

### TL;DR Recap

| What you need | Exact sprite names | Where to get them |
|---------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| **Sprite sheet** | `road-shield-1` … `road-shield-12` (inside the `road_shield` sprite) | `https://github.com/openmaptiles/openmaptiles/tree/master/styles/road_shield/sprite` (or CDN `https://openmaptiles.org/sprites/road_shield`) |
| **How to use** | Host `road_shield.{png,json}` (+ `@2x` files) and set the style’s `sprite` URL to the base name (no extension) | No layer changes needed – the style already points to those names. |

Once the sprite is reachable, the shields appear automatically. Happy mapping!
